agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.agent: Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures
agents.conditions: Pure water to about 70-80 °C

However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.

agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.conditions: Boiling water (stagnant) and 80 °C aerated water tests; service life depends on temperature and oxygen content
agents.finding: Zytel nylon resins are resistant to hot water and steam. Thus, Zytel has found wide uses in such applications as hot water mixing valves, gears and baskets, equipment used for conveying in hot water and parts which must be subjected to steam, as in a sterilization cycle. Factors important to performance: a 15 °C increase in temperature may reduce life by 40-50 %; service life is shorter in oxygen-rich water.
agents.locator: p. 39, 5.3 Resistance of Zytel to hot water and steam

agents.conditions: Florida and Arizona outdoor exposure
agents.finding: Natural and pigmented Zytel nylon resins have only moderate resistance to the effects of sunlight but special weather-resistant compositions retain their properties and appearance for years. Table 5.05 Florida weathering: Zytel 101 NC010 (66 nylon, not stabilized) tensile strength 73 MPa initially, 37 MPa after 6 months, elongation 300 % to 10 %; Zytel 105 BK010A (light stabilized, black) 63 to 62 MPa and 160 % to 60 %.

agents.agent: Water absorption at 50 % RH and 100 % RH
agents.conditions: 23 °C equilibrium
agents.finding: Nylons absorb moisture from the air and 66 nylon equilibrates at about 2,8 % water at 50 % RH and at about 8,5 % at 100 % RH. This plasticizes the nylon, lowering its strength and stiffness but increasing its toughness and elongation. Moisture absorption increases dimensions of 66 nylons by 0,6 % at 50 % RH and about 2,6 % at 100 % RH.

agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.conditions: Boiling water (stagnant) and 80 °C aerated water tests; service life depends on temperature and oxygen content
agents.finding: Zytel nylon resins are resistant to hot water and steam. Thus, Zytel has found wide uses in such applications as hot water mixing valves, gears and baskets, equipment used for conveying in hot water and parts which must be subjected to steam, as in a sterilization cycle. Factors important to performance: a 15 °C increase in temperature may reduce life by 40-50 %; service life is shorter in oxygen-rich water.
agents.locator: p. 39, 5.3 Resistance of Zytel to hot water and steam

agents.conditions: Florida and Arizona outdoor exposure
agents.finding: Natural and pigmented Zytel nylon resins have only moderate resistance to the effects of sunlight but special weather-resistant compositions retain their properties and appearance for years. Table 5.05 Florida weathering: Zytel 101 NC010 (66 nylon, not stabilized) tensile strength 73 MPa initially, 37 MPa after 6 months, elongation 300 % to 10 %; Zytel 105 BK010A (light stabilized, black) 63 to 62 MPa and 160 % to 60 %.

agents.agent: Water absorption at 50 % RH and 100 % RH
agents.conditions: 23 °C equilibrium
agents.finding: Nylons absorb moisture from the air and 66 nylon equilibrates at about 2,8 % water at 50 % RH and at about 8,5 % at 100 % RH. This plasticizes the nylon, lowering its strength and stiffness but increasing its toughness and elongation. Moisture absorption increases dimensions of 66 nylons by 0,6 % at 50 % RH and about 2,6 % at 100 % RH.

agents.conditions: 1.6 mm and 3.2 mm specimens
agents.finding: Zytel 101L: oxygen index 28 % (dry), 31 % (50 % RH); 1,6 mm 94 V2; 3,2 mm 94 V2

agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.conditions: 10 % wt/vol mixture, shaken at 175 rpm at room temperature; some samples stirred at 65 °C
agents.finding: Of the solvents studied, chloroform is the best solvent for quickly preparing 10 % wt/vol solutions of all Ingeo grades and morphologies; 4032D pellets and injection-moulded bars were readily transformed to 10 % wt/vol solutions in chloroform in 2-4 hours at room temperature

agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
agents.conditions: Lengthy exposure
agents.finding: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

agents.conditions: Continuous exposure above 50 °C
agents.finding: All thermoplastic polyester resins will hydrolyze in hot water. The hydrolysis results in polymer degradation and a decrease in the physical properties of the resin. The rate of hydrolysis depends on exposure conditions; primarily time, temperature and the composition of the specific polyester resin. We recommend that parts made from Rynite should not be used in an environment where there is continuous exposure to water at temperatures above 50 °C.

agents.agent: Outdoor weathering (carbon arc X-W Weather-Ometer, Florida and Arizona exposure)
agents.conditions: 10 000 hours X-W Weather-Ometer
agents.finding: Thermoplastic polyester resins rank high, among engineering polymers, for resistance to outdoor weathering... in general, Rynite exhibits good property retention. Overall performance is improved, especially impact strength, by the addition of carbon black (> 0,3 % by weight) to the resin. After 10 000 hours in the X-W Weather-Ometer Rynite 530 NC010 and Rynite 545 NC010 retain over 70 % of their initial tensile strength and 55 % of their original elongation properties.

agents.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
agents.conditions: Lengthy exposure
agents.finding: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

agents.conditions: Not stated
agents.finding: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.

agents.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
agents.conditions: High temperature
agents.finding: Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

agents.agent: Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures
agents.conditions: Pure water to about 70-80 °C
agents.finding: Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

agents.conditions: Wavelengths below 400 nm
agents.finding: Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.

agents.conditions: Not stated
agents.finding: Most VESTAMID compounds are flammable. At mass temperatures above 350 °C flammable gases form through decomposition.
agents.notes: No UL 94 rating for the neat resin is stated. Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.

agents.conditions: 10 % wt/vol mixture, shaken at 175 rpm at room temperature; some samples stirred at 65 °C

agents.agent: Lubricating oils and greases (IRM 901, 902, 903 test oils)
agents.conditions: Immersion at room temperature; 3 weeks at 100 °C
agents.finding: No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. agents.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
agents.conditions: Lengthy exposure
agents.finding: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

agents.conditions: Not stated

In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.

agents.notes: Columns: Elastollan standard ester grades (e.g. 500, 800), Elastollan C 85 A, Elastollan ether grades (e.g. 1100); each at 23 °C and 60 °C, resistance expressed as hours, days, weeks, months or years. Harder products swell less and resist better. A filament's base (ester or ether) is usually not published.

agents.finding: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
